_doc: Plans whose board materials the cloud pipeline cannot fetch. These are SKIPPED EVERYWHERE by pipeline.py. Naming a blocked plan explicitly on the CLI still processes it, which is how the Mac Mini job fetches them from a residential IP. Materials coverage is 137 of 148 while every id here is skipped.
_blocked_by: Why a plan is here, and therefore who can fetch it. Probed 2026-09-01 from a residential IP. THERE ARE TWO INDEPENDENT AXES, and the first pass measured only one: rendering the listing page, and downloading the PDFs it links to. A plan is useful to the Mac Mini only if BOTH work. 'datacentre_ip' -- listing renders AND PDFs download, so Stage 1 fetches it. 'download_403' -- listing renders but the PDF path 403s, to plain requests, to a cookie-carrying session, and to Playwright's own browser request context alike; discovery without download is worthless, so the Mini cannot serve it. 'other' -- the listing page itself 403s from a residential IP, so the block is not IP reputation at all. 'no_materials' -- NOT blocked and not fixable: the page renders from anywhere and simply has no agendas, minutes or packets on it. Nothing to do until the plan starts publishing, and a change of host or selector buys nothing. Results in docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-30-mac-mini-waf-plans.md Task 1.

_how_it_works: Loaded by pipeline.py, which subtracts every id here from the default plan set on every run, local or hosted -- 'blocked_by' does not affect that, so a plan stays skipped in the cloud whatever its reason. Explicit positional plan_ids on the CLI bypass the filter. scripts/waf_blocked_ids.py reads 'blocked_by' to decide which ids the Mac Mini job should name.
